fixes.explanation: The writer doesn't say anything about getting more than anybody else. What he wants for the little children is that they be confident and unashamed before Him at His coming. That's about how they stand before Him, not a bigger box of cookies than the next baker's. And his word to them is to remain in Christ.

Careful, friend, this one is true. The writer says, "If you know that He is righteous, you also know that everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him." That's the very thing you were asked about. Easy one to second-guess, and I second-guess my own recipes all the time.

Yes, ma'am, yes, sir, children of God! The writer says, "Behold what manner of love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God." Look at the word "given." The Father's love is what He has given. My cookie cutter kids called me Papa, but this is a way bigger deal.

That's a nice-sounding title, but it's not the one the writer uses. He says the Father's love has given us this: "…that we should be called children of God." Servants isn't in the verse. Children is the word he picked.

That's it, friend. The writer says, "The reason the world does not know us is that it did not know Him." Think about it like this: if you never met somebody, you won't recognize his kids at the grocery store. The world's trouble starts with not knowing Him, and that's why it doesn't know us.
Powerful doesn't show up in this verse. The writer says, "…purifies himself, just as Christ is pure." That's the comparison he makes. Purifies and pure are cousins, and powerful isn't in the family.

Sickness isn't the word in this verse, friend. The writer says, "…Christ appeared to take away sins…" He's reminding them of something they already know about why Christ appeared. So the thing taken away here is sins, not sickness.

Yes, and the writer says it right after the other part. "…you know that Christ appeared to take away sins, and in Him there is no sin." Not a speck. Those two things sit side by side in the same verse.

This one is true, friend. The writer says, "This is why the Son of God was revealed, to destroy the works of the devil." Right before that, he says the devil has been sinning from the very start. So the Son of God was revealed to destroy what the devil has been doing.

Yes, that's the one. The writer says, "Anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God, nor is anyone who does not love his brother." So he gives two signs of someone who is not of God. Not practicing righteousness is the first, and not loving his brother is the one you picked.
